question: I sold my home in 2025. Do I still report the sale to CRA if it was my principal residence the whole time?
generated_answer: Yes, you still need to report the sale of your principal residence to the CRA, even if it was your principal residence for the entire time you owned it. This is because the CRA requires you to report all capital gains or losses from the sale of property, including your principal residence. However, if the property was your principal residence for the entire time you owned it, you may be eligible to claim the principal residence exemption, which would exempt the capital gain from tax. To claim the exemption, you will need to report the sale on your tax return and complete Form T2091(IND) or T2091(INT) (depending on whether you are a resident or non-resident of Canada), and indicate that the property was your principal residence for the entire time you owned it. The CRA will then review your claim and determine if you are eligible for the exemption. It's always a good idea to consult with a tax professional or accountant to ensure you are meeting all your tax obligations and claiming any available exemptions.
